what: For each product layer (the original is four beds pulled apart and floated — pillow, duvet, sheet, mattress), frames advance with scroll, turning from a top-down angle → eye level → a low angle looking up. The first frame is shown when the layer center touches the bottom edge of the screen and the last frame after rising one more screen height. Frame counts are split separately between the first half and the second half (pillow 0·12·26, duvet 0·24·54, sheet 0·28·54, mattress 0·20·27) and cut to integers, so it steps like a photo sequence. --fx-frame and --fx-tilt are set on the layer so css draws the top and bottom face heights

options.data-frames: Layer attribute — first, middle and last frame numbers, default 0,12,24
options.data-fx-part=\"top\"·\"bottom\": Top and bottom faces within a layer — default css unfolds and folds by --fx-tilt
options.data-fx-part=\"frame\": Frame children inside a layer — if set, only the one with that number shows (a bundle of cuts instead of a sprite)

from.where: index.html .dt-bed — original Brand section Casper__product (sprite frames advance by progress from layer center − (screen height − layer height/2), first half a→m · second half m→b). Instead of the original photo frames, it is redrawn as a drawing that unfolds and folds the top and bottom faces
